title: LoFP
description: Living off the False Positive — an autogenerated collection of false positives sourced from popular rule sets, categorized by ATT&CK techniques, rule source, and data source.

title: LOLDrivers
description: Living Off The Land Drivers — a curated list of Windows drivers used by adversaries to bypass security controls and carry out attacks.

title: GTFOBins
description: A curated list of Unix binaries that can be used to bypass local security restrictions in misconfigured systems.

title: LOLBAS
description: The goal of the LOLBAS project is to document every binary, script, and library that can be used for Living Off The Land techniques.

title: LOTS Project
description: Attackers use popular legitimate domains for phishing, C&C, exfiltration and tool downloads to evade detection. This list catalogs domains that allow user-controlled subdomains.

title: FileSec
description: File extensions being used by attackers — a reference for defenders tracking evolving delivery techniques.

title: MalAPI.io
description: Maps Windows APIs to common techniques used by malware.

title: HijackLibs
description: A curated list of DLL Hijacking candidates for Windows environments.

title: WADComs
description: An interactive cheat sheet of offensive security tools and commands for Windows/AD environments.

title: LOOBins
description: Living Off the Orchard: macOS Binaries — detailed information on built-in macOS binaries and how threat actors abuse them.

title: LOLApps
description: Exploitation isn't limited to command-line binaries — built-in and third-party applications get abused too. This project catalogs those techniques.

title: Bootloaders
description: A curated list of known malicious bootloaders across operating systems, helping defenders stay informed on bootloader-based threats.

title: Bring Your Own Land
description: BYOL — a red-teaming technique where operators carry their own tools instead of relying on what's present on the target.

title: Living Off The Hardware
description: A resource collection for identifying and utilizing malicious hardware and devices.

title: WTFBins
description: A WTFBin is a binary that behaves exactly like malware — except, somehow, it's not.

title: LOFL Project
description: Living Off the Foreign Land — Cmdlets and Binaries (LOFLCABs) that perform activities from the local Windows system against a remote system.

title: Persistence Info
description: Information on Windows persistence mechanisms, organized to make protection and detection more efficient.

title: lolcerts
description: Details of code-signing certificates known to be abused in the wild — stolen or legally-acquired, then used to sign malware.

title: LOTP
description: Catalogs CI/CD tools with lesser-known RCE-by-design features ("foot guns") that enable arbitrary code execution through untrusted changes or workflow injection.

title: lolbins-cti driven
description: Helps cyber defenders understand how LOLBin binaries are used by threat actors during an intrusion, in a graphical and digestible format.

title: LOLESXi
description: A comprehensive list of binaries and scripts natively available in VMware ESXi that adversaries have used in their operations.

title: LOLRMM
description: A curated list of Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools that could potentially be abused by threat actors.

title: LOT Webhooks
description: A community-driven project documenting webhooks that may be exploited for data exfiltration and C2 communications.

title: Project-Lost
description: A curated list of security tools used by adversaries to bypass security controls and carry out attacks.

title: LOT Tunnels
description: Documents digital tunnels that can be abused by threat actors or insiders for data exfiltration, persistence, and shell access.

title: LOLAD
description: A comprehensive collection of Active Directory techniques, commands, and functions usable natively for offensive security operations and red team exercises.

title: LOLC2
description: A collection of C2 frameworks that leverage legitimate services to evade detection.

title: LOLAPI
description: Real-world abused APIs across Windows, cloud, and browser platforms — with detection strategies, mitigation guidance, and red-team POCs.

title: LOLEXFIL
description: A comprehensive catalog of data exfiltration methods with detection patterns, simulation examples, IOC artifacts, and ATT&CK mappings.

title: LOLFSaaS
description: Living Off Free SaaS — a directory of free SaaS platforms used for C2, exfiltration, and adversary tooling, with ATT&CK mappings and detection logic.

title: LOTE
description: Living Off Trusted Email — a quick-reference for leveraging trusted platforms' email features to deliver phishing during social engineering campaigns.

title: LOLSkills
description: Inspects AI agent skill bundles — instructions, scripts, and config — for hidden or harmful behavior before you install them, using Nova and YARA detections with correlated evidence.

title: GTFOArgs
description: A curated list of Unix binaries whose arguments can be exploited for argument injection — enabling shell escapes, privilege escalation, and arbitrary file read/write.

title: LOLGlobs
description: Process execution hidden behind wildcard and glob pattern evasion, catalogued across shells and platforms and mapped to ATT&CK tactics.

title: LOLCreds
description: A reference catalog of default and embedded credentials across products and platforms — where they live, what they look like, and what they unlock.

title: RogueApps
description: OAuth and OIDC applications observed being abused in real attacks, with consent artifacts, indicators, and detection guidance for identity teams.

title: ArgFuscator
description: Documents command-line obfuscation across Windows, Linux, and macOS — which utilities tolerate which mangling, and generates working obfuscated equivalents to test defenses.
